top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, KLOwen, damon ultima brackets, Lightforce, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, self-ligating braces, Twin brackets, SmartSTL
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, rentability, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, staff efficiency, staff satisfaction, diary changes, scheduling, emergencies decrease, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in second and third order movements
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually reduce chair time, appointments, or staff workload, and question whether the investment will pay off. They want proof that DM delivers measurable efficiency and financial benefits in real-world practices, not just theoretical claims.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
Wenig Mitarbeiter, voller Terminkalender, lange Wartezeiten
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for robust, region-specific, and appliance-specific data on ROI and efficiency, especially for non-Invisalign appliances and multi-location or large practices. Comparative studies versus standard recall protocols are especially lacking.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI for clinical observations and remote monitoring
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, class I goal, occlusal assessment, accuracy of scanning, accuracy compared to intraoral scan, FDA application, accuracy of AI detecting eruption, aligner unseat tracking
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI is accurate enough to reliably detect clinical changes, diagnose remotely, or match the judgment of an orthodontist. Some are concerned about regulatory validation and want to see quantitative accuracy data.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
How accurate is SmartSTL AI
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a shortage of head-to-head studies comparing DM’s AI to orthodontist assessments and to other digital tools, especially for specific clinical tasks and regulatory endpoints.
